note.text: Obversion retains the subject and quantity, changes affirmative to negative or negative to affirmative, and replaces the complete predicate by its complement. The complement contains exactly what is outside that class within a fixed universe. Under the standard set-based meanings used here, all the categorical forms are equivalent to their obverses. Complement is not merely an everyday opposite: non-red does not mean only blue. Double complementation restores the original class.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to obvert each categorical form by changing quality and complementing the whole predicate. Builds on: categorical forms, conversion and fixed terms. Leads to: complex eduction without changing a claim’s scope.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: Obversion retains the subject and quantity, changes affirmative to negative or negative to affirmative, and replaces the complete predicate by its complement. The complement contains exactly what is outside that class within a fixed universe. Under the standard set-based meanings used here, all the categorical forms are equivalent to their obverses. Complement is not merely an everyday opposite: non-red does not mean only blue. Double complementation restores the original class.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original models: All S are P becomes No S are non-P. No S are P becomes All S are non-P. Some S are P becomes Some S are not non-P. Some S are not P becomes Some S are non-P. For club members and badge holders, non-(badge holders) means all items outside the badge-holder class within the stated universe.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Keep S fixed. Circle the original quality and change it, retain all or some scope, then complement the entire P term. Check that you have not merely negated the whole sentence. Use the fixed-universe meaning of non-P, not a narrow everyday opposite.

example: retained subject: the unchanged subject term in an obverse.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: S stays the subject when All S are P is obverted.
A becomes E while I becomes O.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve scope, terms and assumptions.
example: Obversion requires exchanging S and P. Correction: The subject remains fixed; conversion exchanges terms.
Complementing P alone completes obversion. Correction: Quality must also change.
The complement of red is exactly blue in every universe. Correction: Many things can be neither red nor blue.
Obverting a universal alone creates a particular witness. Correction: Changing quality and predicate does not add existence.
